The taste of sugar is sweet. It is a primary taste sensation that triggers pleasure centers in the brain and is often associated with energy and reward. Sugar, specifically sucrose, dissolves on the tongue and binds to sweet taste receptors, sending signals to the brain that interpret the flavor as sweet. This sensation is generally considered pleasant in moderate amounts, though excessive consumption can lead to health issues.
